# CLI reference

## `prometheus`

```text
Prometheus Agent

Usage: prometheus [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  chat         Talk to the agent: interactive on a terminal, one-shot with `-z` or when stdin or stdout is not a terminal (the default command)
  version      Print the version and build identity (`--json` for every field, `--verbose` for build details and compiled-in surfaces)
  setup        Set up the profile: model and provider (or a subscription sign-in), secrets, tools, terminal and memory
  doctor       Check the install and profile: one ok / warn / fail line per check; `--fix` performs the enumerated repairs
  debug        Diagnostics: `debug summary` prints a plain-text setup summary for support threads
  config       Read, change, validate and explain the profile's config.toml
  secrets      Store, list and remove the profile's secrets (values never on the command line)
  skills       List, inspect, enable, lint and maintain the profile's skills and skill bundles
  journey      The skills and memories the agent learned, as a timeline; list, delete, edit [aliases: learning, memory-graph]
  memory       Inspect, edit, export and import what the agent remembers (built-in memory)
  grants       List and revoke the profile's permanent capability grants and approvals
  browser      Browser sessions: status, and closing the real browser whose profile real-profile browsing copies
  lsp          Language servers behind the diagnostics of file edits: status, registry, installs, restart
  cron         Scheduled jobs: create, list, pause, run now, inspect runs, replay, doctor and the headless tick
  worktrees    Git worktrees of sessions and subagents: list, sweep and restore archived trees
  vault        The credential vault: logins, cards and addresses the browser fills by handle
  security     Security records of the profile: verify the tamper-evident audit log
  backup       Back up the whole home to a .tar.zst archive, or restore one
  files        Undo a session's file changes, roll a workspace back to a checkpoint, and manage the file snapshot store
  verify       Detect a project's build/test/start recipe and run it
  snapshots    Snapshot and restore the selected profile's critical state
  profile      List, create, select, rename and delete profiles
  sessions     List, search, export and manage the profile's sessions
  logs         Show structured log records of a component (`list` names them)
  usage        Totals of model and metered tool calls from the usage ledger
  prompt       Measure the system prompt and tool schemas a new session would send
  demo         Run the offline demo: the agent fixes a bug in a small ledger repository with the scripted mock provider, in a temporary profile
  trajectory   Render the recorded trajectory of a session
  model        Pick, set, list and inspect the profile's model (no subcommand: the interactive picker)
  providers    Provider routing state: per-route health scores
  moa          List, create, update and delete Mixture of Agents presets (`[moa.presets.<name>]`)
  fallback     List and edit the profile's fallback chain (`[[fallback.chain]]`)
  auth         Add, list and remove provider API keys and subscription sign-ins (an interactive manager without a subcommand on a terminal)
  tools        List the profile's tools and explain one (exposure, capabilities, approvals)
  toolsets     List toolsets and show the tools a toolset resolves to
  approvals    Check how the approval gate treats a command, without running it
  update       Update this install to its channel's newest signed release, check for one (exit 10 when available), change the channel, or roll back
  pause        Emergency pause: no new turns or scheduled jobs on any profile of this home until `pause off` (running turns finish)
  portal       The Nous Portal subscription and its tool gateway routing
  daemon       Run, start, stop and inspect the gateway daemon that owns this home's sessions (one per home; clients attach to it)
  gateway      Messaging adapters of the running daemon and the profile's delivery outbox
  pairing      Approve, deny, list and revoke messaging senders' pairing requests. A code is approved with `prometheus pairing approve <platform> <code>`, the RPC `pairing.approve` from a client attached to the profile, or the admin-only chat command `/pair approve <code>`
  connectors   Hosted app connectors (Gmail, Notion, Linear...) on the Nous connector gateway: list them, list and rename accounts, connect and disconnect accounts
  bridge       The python bridge: sidecar status, logs and restarts, a doctor for the managed runtime and plugin environments, and named side environments for skill scripts
  mcp          MCP servers: add (from a preset or the catalog), list, remove, test and sign in to the profile's servers, pick their tools, show their state, and serve Prometheus tools and skills to MCP clients. With no subcommand on a terminal, an interactive picker
  plugins      Plugins: list, enable and disable them, manage their capability grants, and run the adapter conformance kit (`plugins test-adapter`)
  tui          The full-screen terminal UI, attached to the home's gateway daemon (started when it is not running), or with `--standalone` to an in-process gateway that serves only this TUI
  schema       Print the JSON Schema of a published contract (`subagent-result`)
  rpc          The daemon's client protocol: `rpc schema` prints the schema this binary speaks
  completions  Print a shell completion script (load it from your shell's startup file, for example `source <(prometheus completions zsh)`)
  runtimes     List, install, verify and collect the managed runtimes (Node, CPython, uv, Chromium) shared by every profile
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -V, --version
          Print version

  -m, --model <MODEL>
          Model for this session (`[<provider>/]<model>` or an alias)

      --provider <ID>
          Provider for this session

  -t, --toolsets <LIST>
          Toolsets for this session, comma-separated

  -r, --resume <REF>
          Resume a session by id, id prefix, title or `latest`

  -c, --continue [<NAME>]
          Resume the most recent CLI session started in this directory, or with NAME the newest session of the lineage titled NAME

  -z, --oneshot [<PROMPT>]
          Run one prompt non-interactively and print only the answer (the prompt from this flag, `--prompt-file` or stdin)

      --query <TEXT>
          Start an interactive session with TEXT as its first message, sent verbatim (never run as a slash command)

      --prompt-file <PATH>
          Read the prompt verbatim from PATH (`-` for stdin)

      --image <PATH>
          Attach a local image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP; at most 20 MiB) to the first prompt (repeatable)

      --approvals <MODE>
          Approval mode for this session

          Possible values:
          - manual: Ask for every dangerous call
          - smart:  Pre-screen with an auxiliary model; ask when uncertain
          - off:    No prompts (deny rules and hardline blocks still apply)

      --yolo
          Allow every approval-gated call for this session (deny rules and hardline blocks still apply)

      --egress <MODE>
          Network egress of this session: any public host, only allowed hosts, or none (`security.egress.mode` otherwise)

          Possible values:
          - public:    Any public host; private and metadata ranges denied
          - allowlist: Only `security.egress.allow` and `--allow-host` patterns
          - none:      No outbound connections

      --allow-host <PATTERN>
          Admit this host pattern (`host`, `host:port`, `*.suffix`) in this session, in addition to `security.egress.allow` (repeatable)

      --max-iterations <N>
          Model calls allowed per turn

      --checkpoints
          Record file snapshots and checkpoints for `/undo` and `/rollback` this run, whatever `files.snapshot.enabled` says

      --no-checkpoints
          Record no file snapshots or checkpoints this run

  -w, --worktree [<NAME>]
          Run the session in a new git worktree of the current repository (`.worktrees/NAME` on branch `prometheus/NAME`; a generated name when omitted); with `-r`/`-c` of a session that owns one, reopen it

      --cwd <DIR>
          Working directory of the session (also scopes `-c` and `latest`)

      --in-process
          Run the session in this process instead of attaching to the home's running gateway daemon (which then holds the home: exit 75)

      --tui
          Use the full-screen interface

      --line
          Use the line interface

  -s, --skills <LIST>
          Skills to load at session start, comma-separated (repeatable)

      --source <TAG>
          Integration tag recorded on the session

      --pass-session-id
          Put the session id in the system prompt

      --run-budget <SECS>
          Wall-clock budget of each turn in seconds

      --no-context-files
          Do not load project context files (AGENTS.md and friends)

      --ignore-user-config
          Run with schema defaults and this command line's flags instead of the profile's config.toml (secrets still resolve)

      --ignore-rules
          Skip workspace rule files (AGENTS.md and friends), the identity file, the memory snapshot and preloaded skills

      --usage-file <PATH>
          Write this run's usage as JSON to PATH when it ends, whatever the outcome

      --mock-script <PATH>
          Script for the `mock` provider

      --base-url <URL>
          Endpoint for this invocation only (without `--provider`: provider `custom`); never saved

      --api-key-stdin
          Read the endpoint's API key from stdin; it is held in memory only and sent to the `--base-url` host only

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `prometheus setup`

```text
Set up the profile: model and provider (or a subscription sign-in), secrets, tools, terminal and memory

Usage: prometheus setup [OPTIONS] [SECTION]

Arguments:
  [SECTION]
          Only this section (all but `tools` and `gateway` when omitted)

          Possible values:
          - model:    Provider and model, or a subscription sign-in, and its API key
          - secrets:  The secrets the configured providers need
          - tools:    Toolsets per surface and tool providers
          - terminal: The terminal backend
          - memory:   The memory stores
          - gateway:  Messaging adapters (with the gateway)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --non-interactive
          Take values from `--set` and secrets from the environment instead of asking; a missing required value exits 78

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --reset-onboarding
          Clear the onboarding state (offered setup, shown tips, tour steps)

      --portal
          Sign in to the Nous Portal, make `nous` the main provider and offer to route every tool category through its tool gateway

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `prometheus doctor`

```text
Check the install and profile: one ok / warn / fail line per check; `--fix` performs the enumerated repairs

Usage: prometheus doctor [OPTIONS] [GROUP]

Arguments:
  [GROUP]
          Only this group: home, config, secrets, store, daemon, sandbox, terminal, runtimes, plugins, observability, network, providers or security

Options:
      --fix
          Perform the enumerated repairs (permissions, stale run files, the full-text index, pending config migrations) and print each

      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --online
          Allow network probes (provider reachability, IPv6)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --strict
          Treat warnings as failures; `doctor security --strict` exits 77 on any downgrade

      --all-profiles
          Check every profile of the home

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --ack <ADVISORY_ID>
          Silence the startup warning of a supply-chain advisory (added to `security.acked_advisories`); `doctor security` still shows it

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus config`

```text
Read, change, validate and explain the profile's config.toml

Usage: prometheus config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  path        Print the path of the profile's config.toml
  show        Print config.toml, or with --effective every effective value
  get         Print the effective value of a key
  set         Set a key in config.toml (the value is typed by the key's schema)
  unset       Remove a key from config.toml so its default applies
  edit        Edit config.toml in $VISUAL / $EDITOR; the result is validated before it is saved
  validate    Validate config.toml (exit 0 when valid, 78 when not)
  explain     Explain a key: type, default, effective value, source, apply class
  fix-models  List config keys and cron job pins naming a deprecated or retired model with their replacements; nothing changes without --apply
  schema      Print the config.toml JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)
  docs        Print the configuration reference (Markdown)
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text

Usage: prometheus config set [OPTIONS] <KEY> <VALUE>

Arguments:
  <KEY>
```

## `prometheus skills`

```text
List, inspect, enable, lint and maintain the profile's skills and skill bundles

Usage: prometheus skills [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list             List the profile's skills with category, source and status (shadowed copies marked)
  show             Show one skill: where it comes from, its status, its files and its SKILL.md
  enable           Enable a skill (from the next session)
  disable          Disable a skill (from the next session); `prometheus-agent` cannot be disabled
  lint             Check skills against the authoring rules (all of the profile's when no path is given)
  trust            Load the skills of a git checkout (`.prometheus/skills`, `.agents/skills`) in new sessions
  eject            Copy a bundled skill into the profile as an editable copy that shadows it
  diff             Show how an ejected copy differs from the current bundled version
  reset            Remove an ejected copy so the name resolves to the bundled skill again
  doctor           Report skills that do not load (path, line, reason) and quarantined project skills
  reload           Rescan every skill root and bundle; report added, removed and changed skills since the last reload
  bundles          Manage skill bundles (`<profile>/skill-bundles/<slug>.toml`)
  pending          Review skill writes staged by `skills.write_approval` (default: list them)
  opt-out          Hide every bundled skill from this profile across upgrades (`prometheus-agent` stays)
  opt-in           Show bundled skills again (the default)
  list-modified    List ejected skills whose content differs from their recorded origin
  repair-official  Re-record the provenance of official catalog installs that match the embedded copy
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus skills help`

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: prometheus skills help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list             List the profile's skills with category, source and status (shadowed copies marked)
  show             Show one skill: where it comes from, its status, its files and its SKILL.md
  enable           Enable a skill (from the next session)
  disable          Disable a skill (from the next session); `prometheus-agent` cannot be disabled
  lint             Check skills against the authoring rules (all of the profile's when no path is given)
  trust            Load the skills of a git checkout (`.prometheus/skills`, `.agents/skills`) in new sessions
  eject            Copy a bundled skill into the profile as an editable copy that shadows it
  diff             Show how an ejected copy differs from the current bundled version
  reset            Remove an ejected copy so the name resolves to the bundled skill again
  doctor           Report skills that do not load (path, line, reason) and quarantined project skills
  reload           Rescan every skill root and bundle; report added, removed and changed skills since the last reload
  bundles          Manage skill bundles (`<profile>/skill-bundles/<slug>.toml`)
  pending          Review skill writes staged by `skills.write_approval` (default: list them)
  opt-out          Hide every bundled skill from this profile across upgrades (`prometheus-agent` stays)
  opt-in           Show bundled skills again (the default)
  list-modified    List ejected skills whose content differs from their recorded origin
  repair-official  Re-record the provenance of official catalog installs that match the embedded copy
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

## `prometheus journey`

```text
The skills and memories the agent learned, as a timeline; list, delete, edit

Usage: prometheus journey [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list    The nodes, one per line: id, kind, origin, created, title
  delete  Remove a node: a skill is archived (restorable), a memory entry is removed as a revertible `user` revision
  edit    Edit a node in `$EDITOR`: a skill's `SKILL.md` or an entry's text, applied through the usual validation and scan
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --since <DURATION|DATE>
          Only what was learned since: a duration (`2h`, `3d`, `1w`) or a date (`2026-11-01`)

      --play
          Animate the build-up, one node per frame

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --fps <N>
          Frames a second of `--play`

          [default: 8]

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --width <W>
          Columns of the view

      --height <H>
          Rows of the constellation above the timeline (0 for none)

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus memory`

```text
Inspect, edit, export and import what the agent remembers (built-in memory)

Usage: prometheus memory [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status   Show whether built-in memory is enabled, each store's usage and pending changes
  list     List entries (dormant ones only with --all)
  show     Show one entry in full (blocked entries show their raw text here)
  add      Add an entry (from the next session's snapshot)
  rm       Remove an entry
  pin      Pin an entry
  unpin    Unpin an entry
  edit     Edit entries as Markdown in $VISUAL / $EDITOR; the result is applied as one batch after showing the diff
  export   Print every entry as Markdown (the edit view) or JSONL
  import   Import a Markdown or JSONL export, or a Hermes MEMORY.md / USER.md (entries separated by §)
  pending  List memory changes staged for approval
  approve  Apply a staged change (`all` for every one)
  reject   Drop a staged change (`all` for every one)
  log      List memory revisions, oldest first
  diff     Show memory changes as a unified diff per entry
  revert   Undo a revision (recorded as a new revision with origin user)
  search   Rank archival entries for a query as recall would
  setup    Set up an external memory provider: its settings go to config.toml, its secrets to the secrets store; takes effect from the next session
  off      Use built-in memory only (memory.provider = "builtin")
  reset    Delete every entry of a store
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text
Print every entry as Markdown (the edit view) or JSONL

Usage: prometheus memory export [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          The format

          Possible values:
          - md:    The Markdown view `memory edit` opens
          - jsonl: One JSON object per entry

          [default: md]

      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --target <TARGET>
          Only this store

          Possible values:
          - memory: The agent's own notes
          - user:   The user profile

  -o, --output <FILE>
          Write to this file instead of stdout

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `prometheus memory import`

```text
Import a Markdown or JSONL export, or a Hermes MEMORY.md / USER.md (entries separated by §)

Usage: prometheus memory import [OPTIONS] <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          The file

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --target <TARGET>
          The store a Hermes file belongs to (default: from the file name)

          Possible values:
          - memory: The agent's own notes
          - user:   The user profile

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --tier <TIER>
          The tier of entries from a Hermes file

          Possible values:
          - core:     Shown in the system prompt (budgeted)
          - archival: Recalled per turn

          [default: core]

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `prometheus memory help`

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: prometheus memory help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status   Show whether built-in memory is enabled, each store's usage and pending changes
  list     List entries (dormant ones only with --all)
  show     Show one entry in full (blocked entries show their raw text here)
  add      Add an entry (from the next session's snapshot)
  rm       Remove an entry
  pin      Pin an entry
  unpin    Unpin an entry
  edit     Edit entries as Markdown in $VISUAL / $EDITOR; the result is applied as one batch after showing the diff
  export   Print every entry as Markdown (the edit view) or JSONL
  import   Import a Markdown or JSONL export, or a Hermes MEMORY.md / USER.md (entries separated by §)
  pending  List memory changes staged for approval
  approve  Apply a staged change (`all` for every one)
  reject   Drop a staged change (`all` for every one)
  log      List memory revisions, oldest first
  diff     Show memory changes as a unified diff per entry
  revert   Undo a revision (recorded as a new revision with origin user)
  search   Rank archival entries for a query as recall would
  setup    Set up an external memory provider: its settings go to config.toml, its secrets to the secrets store; takes effect from the next session
  off      Use built-in memory only (memory.provider = "builtin")
  reset    Delete every entry of a store
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

## `prometheus cron`

```text
Scheduled jobs: create, list, pause, run now, inspect runs, replay, doctor and the headless tick

Usage: prometheus cron [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list         The jobs: id, name, schedule, state, next run and last status
  add          Create a job; the schedule is echoed with its next three instants and saved only after confirmation
  edit         Change a job; a new schedule is echoed and confirmed again
  pause        Stop a job from firing until it is resumed
  resume       Fire a paused job again, from now
  run          Run a job now, in the foreground (its schedule and state are untouched)
  remove       Delete a job (its run records are kept under run retention) [alias: rm]
  runs         A job's runs, newest first
  show-run     One run in full: times, status, error, session, cost and output
  replay       Re-execute a recorded run without delivering it
  incidents    Failure incidents, newest activity first; `ack <id>` silences one
  notepad      A job's notepad: `list` (default), `get <key>`, `set <key> <value>`, `delete <key>`
  suggestions  Suggested automations: `list` (default), `accept <n> [--yes]`, `dismiss <n>`, `catalog` (adds the curated starters), `clear`
  status       Job counts, the next due job and who ticks the profile
  doctor       Trigger, tick lease, due-but-unfired occurrences, jobs in error, undelivered outbox rows and every `cron.*` setting; exits 1 when a job is in error or a delivery outcome is unknown
  tick         Run one tick in this process (for OS schedulers); does nothing while a gateway daemon owns scheduling
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus cron add`

```text
Create a job; the schedule is echoed with its next three instants and saved only after confirmation

Usage: prometheus cron add [OPTIONS] [SCHEDULE] [PROMPT]

Arguments:
  [SCHEDULE]
          `every <duration>`, a cron expression or day/time phrase, an RFC 3339 time, `at <time>`, `tomorrow at <time>` or `in <duration>`

  [PROMPT]
          The prompt (same as `--prompt`)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --name <NAME>
          Display name (default: the prompt's first 50 characters)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --prompt <PROMPT>
          The self-contained prompt each run starts with

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --skill <NAME>
          A skill preloaded into each run (repeatable)

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --script <SCRIPT>
          A script in the profile's `scripts/` directory; its output joins the prompt

      --no-agent
          The script is the whole job: its output is delivered as is

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --deliver <TARGET>
          Where output goes (repeatable): `local`, `origin`, `none`, `<platform>`, `<platform>:<chat_id>[:<thread_id>]`, `bot_chat[:<profile>]`

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --toolsets <TOOLSETS>
          Toolsets of each run (comma-separated; `none` for no tools)

      --memory <MEMORY>
          `read_only` (default), `read_write` or `off`

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

      --grace <GRACE>
          How late a run may start (`0s` to `24h`)

      --idle-timeout <IDLE_TIMEOUT>
          Interrupt a run idle this long (`0s` = unlimited)

      --wall-timeout <WALL_TIMEOUT>
          Interrupt a run after this long (`0s` = unlimited)

      --repeat <REPEAT>
          Runs before the job completes

      --model <MODEL>
          Pin this model

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          The provider of `--model`

      --pin
          Pin the profile's current main model and provider (ignored with `--model`)

      --unpin
          Follow `cron.model` (else the main model) again

      --reasoning-effort <LEVEL>
          Pin a reasoning level: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max (`""` clears)

      --workdir <DIR>
          An existing absolute directory the run works in, loading its project context files (`""` clears)

      --failure-deliver <TARGET>
          Where failure notices go instead of `--deliver` (repeatable; `""` clears)

      --attach-to-session <BOOL>
          Link deliveries to a conversation a reply continues (`true` or `false`; unset follows `cron.continuable`)

          [possible values: true, false]

      --script-secret <NAME>
          A secret passed to the script's environment (repeatable; `""` clears)

      --interpreter <PATH>
          The absolute interpreter of a `.py` script (`""` clears)

      --monitor-script <SCRIPT>
          A monitor script in `scripts/`: the agent runs only when its output changes (`""` clears)

      --monitor-url <URL>
          A monitored http(s) URL: the agent runs only when the page changes (`""` clears)

      --context-from <JOB>
          A job whose latest output is prepended to the prompt (repeatable; `""` clears)

      --continuity
          Prepend this job's own previous report

      --no-continuity
          Stop prepending this job's own previous report

      --tz <ZONE>
          The IANA zone the schedule runs in (default `cron.timezone`)

      --nl <TEXT>
          A free-form schedule for the auxiliary model to translate

      --yes
          Save without asking

      --paused
          Create it paused: nothing fires until `cron resume`

      --paused-reason <PAUSED_REASON>
          Why it is paused (default `Created paused; awaiting operator approval.`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus cron help`

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: prometheus cron help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list         The jobs: id, name, schedule, state, next run and last status
  add          Create a job; the schedule is echoed with its next three instants and saved only after confirmation
  edit         Change a job; a new schedule is echoed and confirmed again
  pause        Stop a job from firing until it is resumed
  resume       Fire a paused job again, from now
  run          Run a job now, in the foreground (its schedule and state are untouched)
  remove       Delete a job (its run records are kept under run retention)
  runs         A job's runs, newest first
  show-run     One run in full: times, status, error, session, cost and output
  replay       Re-execute a recorded run without delivering it
  incidents    Failure incidents, newest activity first; `ack <id>` silences one
  notepad      A job's notepad: `list` (default), `get <key>`, `set <key> <value>`, `delete <key>`
  suggestions  Suggested automations: `list` (default), `accept <n> [--yes]`, `dismiss <n>`, `catalog` (adds the curated starters), `clear`
  status       Job counts, the next due job and who ticks the profile
  doctor       Trigger, tick lease, due-but-unfired occurrences, jobs in error, undelivered outbox rows and every `cron.*` setting; exits 1 when a job is in error or a delivery outcome is unknown
  tick         Run one tick in this process (for OS schedulers); does nothing while a gateway daemon owns scheduling
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

```text
Back up the whole home to a .tar.zst archive, or restore one

Usage: prometheus backup [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create   Write a backup of the whole home (default: <home>/backups/prometheus-<UTC time>.tar.zst)
  restore  Restore an archive after verifying every member (-p/--profile NAME restores only that profile)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus backup create`

```text
Write a backup of the whole home (default: <home>/backups/prometheus-<UTC time>.tar.zst)

Usage: prometheus backup create [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -o, --output <FILE>
          Write the archive here instead

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --quick
          Only critical state: config, secrets, grants, state.db, cron jobs, pairing data

      --label <TEXT>
          Label added to the default file name

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --keep <N>
          Default-named backups to keep in <home>/backups

          [default: 3]

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus verify`

```text
Detect a project's build/test/start recipe and run it

Usage: prometheus verify [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]
          The project directory (default: the current directory)

Options:
      --detect-only
          Print the detected recipe as JSON and run nothing

      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --save
          Write the detected recipe to `.prometheus/environment.json`

      --phase <PHASE>
          Run only these phases (repeatable)

          [possible values: bootstrap, build, test, start]

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --skip-start
          Skip the start phase

      --port <PORT>
          The port the start phase listens on

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

      --timeout <TIMEOUT>
          Seconds each phase may run

          [default: 600]

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --ready-timeout <READY_TIMEOUT>
          Seconds the start phase may take to listen

          [default: 60]

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus profile`

```text
List, create, select, rename and delete profiles

Usage: prometheus profile [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list    List the profiles; the active one is marked
  create  Create a profile, optionally copying another one once
  alias   Write a launcher that runs `prometheus -p <name> "$@"` into your bin directory (~/.local/bin, or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Prometheus\bin)
  export  Export a profile as a .tar.zst archive (no secrets, sessions or logs unless asked)
  import  Create a profile from an archive `profile export` wrote
  use     Make a profile the one used without -p (`use default` clears the choice)
  show    Show a profile (default: the selected one)
  rename  Rename a profile
  delete  Delete a profile and everything in it (asks to type its name unless --yes)
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)
```

## `prometheus sessions`

```text
List, search, export and manage the profile's sessions

Usage: prometheus sessions [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  browse           Pick a session interactively (status tags, search) and resume it
  resume           Resume a session (id, id prefix or title) in a chat; a turn the process stopped during is resumed, closed or offered by `agent.resume_on_crash`
  list             List sessions, most recently active first
  show             Show a session (id, id prefix or title)
  search           Full-text search over the profile's messages
  rename           Set a session's title
  pin              Pin a session (pinned sessions are never pruned)
  unpin            Unpin a session
  archive          Archive a session (hidden from the default listing)
  unarchive        Unarchive a session
  tree             Show a session's lineage tree (forks, continuations, delegates)
  fork             Fork a session: a new session with its active messages up to --at
  siblings         List the other children of a session's parent (forks, continuations)
  import           Import a JSONL export (all-or-none; ids must be new unless --remap-ids)
  recover          Copy every readable row of state.db into a new clean store (needs the store closed)
  journal-mode     Switch state.db's journal mode offline (delete for filesystems without shared memory)
  refresh-prompts  Rebuild the stored system prompt of sessions at their next turn
  retitle          Regenerate automatic titles with the title model (user titles are kept)
  stats            Show a session's and its lineage's message and token totals
  export           Export sessions (jsonl, md, html, prompts or trace)
  delete           Delete a session (asks for confirmation unless --yes)
  prune            Delete ended, unpinned sessions inactive for longer than --older-than days
  rewind           Rewind a session to a user message (soft delete; --restore undoes it)
  repair           Rebuild the derived search indexes from the stored messages
  vacuum           Compact state.db and truncate its write-ahead log
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text
          - oldest: Oldest first
```

```text
Unarchive a session

Usage: prometheus sessions unarchive [OPTIONS] <SESSION>

Arguments:
  <SESSION>
          Session id, id prefix or title

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus sessions export`

```text
Export sessions (jsonl, md, html, prompts or trace)

Usage: prometheus sessions export [OPTIONS] [SESSIONS]...

Arguments:
  [SESSIONS]...
          Sessions to export (id, id prefix or title)

Options:
      --all
          Export every session

      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - jsonl:   Portable JSONL (header, session, messages, usage, lineage)
          - md:      Readable Markdown transcript, tool calls collapsed
          - html:    Self-contained HTML page
          - prompts: Only the user messages, one JSON line each
          - trace:   Trajectory grammar JSONL

          [default: jsonl]

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --include-inactive
          Include rewound and compacted messages

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --with-blobs
          Embed the blobs (attachments) the messages reference, base64 (jsonl)

      --redact
          Replace secrets and credential-shaped text with [REDACTED]

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -o, --output <FILE>
          Write to this file instead of stdout

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `prometheus sessions help`

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: prometheus sessions help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  browse           Pick a session interactively (status tags, search) and resume it
  resume           Resume a session (id, id prefix or title) in a chat; a turn the process stopped during is resumed, closed or offered by `agent.resume_on_crash`
  list             List sessions, most recently active first
  show             Show a session (id, id prefix or title)
  search           Full-text search over the profile's messages
  rename           Set a session's title
  pin              Pin a session (pinned sessions are never pruned)
  unpin            Unpin a session
  archive          Archive a session (hidden from the default listing)
  unarchive        Unarchive a session
  tree             Show a session's lineage tree (forks, continuations, delegates)
  fork             Fork a session: a new session with its active messages up to --at
  siblings         List the other children of a session's parent (forks, continuations)
  import           Import a JSONL export (all-or-none; ids must be new unless --remap-ids)
  recover          Copy every readable row of state.db into a new clean store (needs the store closed)
  journal-mode     Switch state.db's journal mode offline (delete for filesystems without shared memory)
  refresh-prompts  Rebuild the stored system prompt of sessions at their next turn
  retitle          Regenerate automatic titles with the title model (user titles are kept)
  stats            Show a session's and its lineage's message and token totals
  export           Export sessions (jsonl, md, html, prompts or trace)
  delete           Delete a session (asks for confirmation unless --yes)
  prune            Delete ended, unpinned sessions inactive for longer than --older-than days
  rewind           Rewind a session to a user message (soft delete; --restore undoes it)
  repair           Rebuild the derived search indexes from the stored messages
  vacuum           Compact state.db and truncate its write-ahead log
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

## `prometheus logs`

```text
Show structured log records of a component (`list` names them)

Usage: prometheus logs [OPTIONS] [COMPONENT]

Arguments:
  [COMPONENT]
          Component to show (default `agent`), or `list` for every component and its file

          [possible values: agent, errors, gateway, adapter, cron, kanban, mcp, plugins, sandbox, providers, rpc, update, migrate, evolve, eval, list]

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -n, --lines <N>
          Show the last N matching records; 0 shows all

          [default: 50]

  -f, --follow
          Keep printing new records until interrupted (exit 130)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --level <LEVEL>
          Least severe level to show

          Possible values:
          - error: Errors only
          - warn:  Warnings and errors
          - info:  Informational and above
          - debug: Debug and above
          - trace: Everything

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --since <S>
          Records since `<N>[smhd]` ago or an RFC 3339 time

      --session <ID>
          Only records of this session

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

      --root <ID>
          Only records of the sessions of this root lineage

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider
```

## `prometheus usage`

```text
Totals of model and metered tool calls from the usage ledger

Usage: prometheus usage [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --since <S>
          Calls since `<N>[smhd]` ago or an RFC 3339 time

          [default: 30d]

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --until <S>
          Calls before `<N>[smhd]` ago or an RFC 3339 time (default: now)

      --by <BY>
          One row per group

          Possible values:
          - root:     Root session of the lineage
          - session:  Session that made the call
          - model:    Provider and model
          - provider: Provider
          - purpose:  Purpose (`main`, `auxiliary.title`, `compression`...)
          - day:      Calendar day in the profile's time zone
          - profile:  Profile
          - billing:  Billing source (`subscription:<provider>/<label>`, `api_key:<provider>/<label>`, `local`...)

          [default: day]

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --session <ID>
          Only this session and its descendants (a root: its whole lineage)

      --all-profiles
          Every profile, each through its own scope, with a grand total

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

```text
Usage: prometheus fallback [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list    List the chain in order
  add     Validate a route and append it (no argument: the model picker)
  remove  Remove an entry by its 1-based position or `<provider>/<model>`
  clear   Remove every entry
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus auth`

```text
Add, list and remove provider API keys and subscription sign-ins (an interactive manager without a subcommand on a terminal)

Usage: prometheus auth [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add       Store an API key (read from a hidden prompt or stdin) or sign in to a subscription
  list      List every credential: provider, label, kind, source and status (never key or token material)
  status    One provider's credentials, sign-in flows and plan notes
  remove    Delete a credential (and revoke a sign-in's refresh token where the provider offers revocation) [alias: rm]
  priority  Move an API key of the pool to a 0-based position (the order `fill_first` takes them in); the others are renumbered
  reset     Clear benches and cooldowns (every credential of the provider, or one); running sessions use them on their next request
  refresh   Refresh sign-in tokens now and return them to rotation
  logout    Remove every subscription sign-in of a provider
  usage     Show a subscription's account usage windows without starting a session (exit 1 when nothing can be shown)
  import    Copy another tool's sign-in into the secrets store
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus auth add`

```text
Store an API key (read from a hidden prompt or stdin) or sign in to a subscription

Usage: prometheus auth add [OPTIONS] <PROVIDER>

Arguments:
  <PROVIDER>
          Provider id or alias

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --type <TYPE>
          Credential type (default: `oauth` for sign-in-only providers, else `api_key`)

          Possible values:
          - api_key: An API key
          - oauth:   A subscription or OAuth sign-in

      --label <LABEL>
          Label of this credential (default `default`)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --browser
          Sign in through the browser (PKCE on a loopback redirect)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --device
          Sign in with a device code

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --priority <N>
          Put the new API key at this 0-based position of the pool order

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `prometheus tools`

```text
List the profile's tools and explain one (exposure, capabilities, approvals)

Usage: prometheus tools [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  configure   Enable or disable toolsets per surface and choose tool providers, interactively
  enable      Enable a toolset from the next session
  disable     Disable a toolset from the next session
  provider    Choose the provider of a tool category (web search, web extract, browser, image generation, TTS, STT, video, X search)
  list        Every registered tool with its toolset and exposure verdict (`exposed` or a reason code) for the profile's configured toolsets, or as a session froze them (`--session`)
  explain     A tool's schema, owner, capabilities, effect, claims, timeout, result budget and the approval rules that apply to it [alias: show]
  toolsets    The toolsets, as `prometheus toolsets list`
  summary     Per surface: the toolsets its sessions start from, the provider of each tool category they use and every selected tool that is not available, with its reason
  post-setup  Run the setup steps a toolset still needs: install the managed runtimes it uses (after confirmation) and point to the sign-ins it needs
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON
```


## `prometheus approvals test`

```text
Run a command line through the approval gate order (hardline, self-termination, deny rules, bypass, allowlist, dangerous-pattern and content detectors) without executing it, asking anyone or saving anything

Usage: prometheus approvals test [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>...

Arguments:
  <COMMAND>...
          The command line, after `--`

Options:
      --backend <NAME>
          Execution backend to assume (default: `terminal.backend`); hardline and deny rules apply on every backend

      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --mode <MODE>
          Approval mode to assume (default: `approvals.mode`)

          Possible values:
          - manual: Ask for every dangerous call
          - smart:  Pre-screen with the guardian model, asking a human when it cannot decide
          - off:    Bypass prompts; hardline and deny rules still block

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --context <CONTEXT>
          Context to assume; unattended contexts answer from their typed mode

          Possible values:
          - interactive:  A human can answer
          - cron:         A cron job (`approvals.cron_mode`)
          - single_query: `chat -z` (`approvals.single_query_mode`)
          - unattended:   Webhook/API surfaces (`approvals.unattended_mode`)

          [default: interactive]

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `prometheus update`

```text
Update this install to its channel's newest signed release, check for one (exit 10 when available), change the channel, or roll back

Usage: prometheus update [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --check
          Only check: print the newest release and exit 10 when it is newer

      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --status
          Print the install's owner, channel, version and last update; no network request

      --channel <CHANNEL>
          Use this channel (`stable` or `canary`) for this run only

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --set-channel <CHANNEL>
          Persist the install's channel (`stable` or `canary`)

      --allow-downgrade
          Install the channel's newest release even when it is older than this build (for example after leaving canary)

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

      --rollback
          Put back the binary the last update replaced (`prometheus.prev`)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --restore-snapshots
          With `--rollback`: also restore the pre-update snapshots, losing the sessions created since the update (asks first)

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

  -y, --yes
          Confirm `--restore-snapshots` without asking

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

      --backup
          Also write a full home archive before the swap (`update.pre_update_backup = "full"` for this run)

      --no-backup
          Skip the pre-update backup for this run (a store migration still gets its pre-migration snapshot)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus daemon`

```text
Run, start, stop and inspect the gateway daemon that owns this home's sessions (one per home; clients attach to it)

Usage: prometheus daemon [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run                Run the daemon in the foreground (what `start` launches)
  start              Start the daemon in the background; does nothing when it runs
  ensure             Start the daemon when it is not running and print its endpoint (with `--json`: one object for clients that spawn it)
  stop               Stop the daemon after its running turns finish
  restart            Replace the daemon (after a binary update): drain running turns, stop it and start this binary's daemon
  status             Print the daemon's process state
  install-service    Install a per-user supervisor unit that starts the daemon at login (no administrator rights); `--system --run-as-user` installs a boot-time unit instead (root only)
  uninstall-service  Stop and remove the unit `install-service` installed
  help               Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

## `prometheus gateway`

```text
Messaging adapters of the running daemon and the profile's delivery outbox

Usage: prometheus gateway [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status          Print each served profile's messaging adapters and their state
  reload          Start the adapters served profiles enable that are not running (running adapters and conversations are untouched)
  platforms       Print each loaded adapter's capability descriptor (limits, unit, media, interactive tier, optional capabilities)
  stop            Stop the daemon that serves this profile's adapters (releasing their platform credentials), after its running turns finish
  outbox          The durable delivery outbox of the selected profile
  send            Send one message to a chat without an agent turn (through the daemon's outbox when it runs)
  list            List every running Prometheus daemon of this OS user, whatever its home
  enroll          Enroll this home with a relay connector using a one-time token
  slack-manifest  Print (or write) a Slack app manifest for Socket Mode with one slash command per gateway command
  whatsapp        WhatsApp linked-device setup
  pause           Stop dispatching one adapter's inbound messages (they are acknowledged and dropped) without disconnecting it; kept across restarts
  resume          Clear an adapter's pause and reconnect backoff and reconnect it now
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode

      --accept-hooks
```

```text
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus gateway help`

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: prometheus gateway help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status          Print each served profile's messaging adapters and their state
  reload          Start the adapters served profiles enable that are not running (running adapters and conversations are untouched)
  platforms       Print each loaded adapter's capability descriptor (limits, unit, media, interactive tier, optional capabilities)
  stop            Stop the daemon that serves this profile's adapters (releasing their platform credentials), after its running turns finish
  outbox          The durable delivery outbox of the selected profile
  send            Send one message to a chat without an agent turn (through the daemon's outbox when it runs)
  list            List every running Prometheus daemon of this OS user, whatever its home
  enroll          Enroll this home with a relay connector using a one-time token
  slack-manifest  Print (or write) a Slack app manifest for Socket Mode with one slash command per gateway command
  whatsapp        WhatsApp linked-device setup
  pause           Stop dispatching one adapter's inbound messages (they are acknowledged and dropped) without disconnecting it; kept across restarts
  resume          Clear an adapter's pause and reconnect backoff and reconnect it now
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

## `prometheus mcp`

```text
MCP servers: add (from a preset or the catalog), list, remove, test and sign in to the profile's servers, pick their tools, show their state, and serve Prometheus tools and skills to MCP clients. With no subcommand on a terminal, an interactive picker

Usage: prometheus mcp [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add      Add a server: `--command <program> [--args ...]` for a local (stdio) server run in the sandbox, `--url <url>` for a streamable HTTP server, or `--preset <name>`; the server is probed and, on a terminal, its tool checklist offered. Its tools join sessions started afterwards
  list     Every configured server: transport, command or URL, trust and whether it is enabled
  remove   Remove a server [alias: rm]
  test     Start a server and list its tools: handshake, tool count and latency (exit 69 when it does not answer)
  tools    Re-open a server's tool checklist; writes `tools.include` only when not every tool is selected
  login    Sign in to an `auth = "oauth"` server (prints the authorization URL; paste the redirect URL when the browser cannot reach this machine)
  reauth   Forget a server's sign-in and sign in again
  catalog  The MCP servers of the plugin catalog
  install  Install an MCP server from the catalog (disabled until you enable it)
  status   Start every enabled server and show its state, tool count and why it is unavailable
  serve    Serve this profile's `mcp_server.expose_toolsets` (default: the read-only skill tools) as MCP tools and its skills as MCP prompts and resources, on stdio or streamable HTTP
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus mcp add`

```text
Add a server: `--command <program> [--args ...]` for a local (stdio) server run in the sandbox, `--url <url>` for a streamable HTTP server, or `--preset <name>`; the server is probed and, on a terminal, its tool checklist offered. Its tools join sessions started afterwards

Usage: prometheus mcp add [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>
          The server's name (letters, digits, `_` and `-`); its tools are named `mcp__<name>__<tool>`

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --url <URL>
          The streamable HTTP endpoint

      --command <COMMAND>
          The program of a local (stdio) server

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --args <ARGS>...
          The program's arguments

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --preset <PRESET>
          A transport preset (`codex`: `codex mcp-server`); explicit flags win over it

          Possible values:
          - codex: OpenAI Codex as an MCP server: `codex mcp-server`

      --env <KEY=VALUE>
          An environment variable of a stdio server (`KEY=value`; repeat)

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --env-secret <NAME>
          A secrets-store name passed to a stdio server as a variable of the same name (repeat)

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

      --auth <AUTH>
          How an HTTP server authenticates: `header` (the `--auth-secret` bearer token) or `oauth` (sign in with `prometheus mcp login`)

          Possible values:
          - header: The `--auth-secret` bearer token
          - oauth:  OAuth 2.1 (sign in with `prometheus mcp login <name>`)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --auth-secret <NAME>
          The secrets-store name of an HTTP server's bearer token

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

      --trust <TRUST>
          `untrusted` (default): tools that are not read-only need approval

          Possible values:
          - full:      Trusted like built-in tools
          - untrusted: Tools that are not read-only need approval

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `prometheus mcp help`

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: prometheus mcp help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add      Add a server: `--command <program> [--args ...]` for a local (stdio) server run in the sandbox, `--url <url>` for a streamable HTTP server, or `--preset <name>`; the server is probed and, on a terminal, its tool checklist offered. Its tools join sessions started afterwards
  list     Every configured server: transport, command or URL, trust and whether it is enabled
  remove   Remove a server
  test     Start a server and list its tools: handshake, tool count and latency (exit 69 when it does not answer)
  tools    Re-open a server's tool checklist; writes `tools.include` only when not every tool is selected
  login    Sign in to an `auth = "oauth"` server (prints the authorization URL; paste the redirect URL when the browser cannot reach this machine)
  reauth   Forget a server's sign-in and sign in again
  catalog  The MCP servers of the plugin catalog
  install  Install an MCP server from the catalog (disabled until you enable it)
  status   Start every enabled server and show its state, tool count and why it is unavailable
  serve    Serve this profile's `mcp_server.expose_toolsets` (default: the read-only skill tools) as MCP tools and its skills as MCP prompts and resources, on stdio or streamable HTTP
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```
