## `prometheus plugins`

```text
Plugins: list, enable and disable them, manage their capability grants, and run the adapter conformance kit (`plugins test-adapter`)

Usage: prometheus plugins [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  install        Install a plugin: a catalog id (its pinned ref), a `.pmtpkg` file, or a Git URL with `--ref <full commit SHA>`
  search         Catalog entries matching a word
  browse         Every catalog entry, by tier and category
  show           A plugin's details: installed state, worlds, capabilities and provenance, and its catalog entry
  list           Every discovered plugin: id, version, kind, source, state (`loaded`, `disabled`, `unadopted` or `error`) and why it does not load
  enable         Enable a plugin: shows its capabilities and asks you to approve them (non-interactively, `--grant all` or `--grant <cap>,...` approves; otherwise exits 4). It loads in sessions started afterwards
  disable        Disable a plugin (it keeps its grants)
  update         Update a plugin, or every plugin whose catalog ref or package moved; one asking for new capabilities keeps its current version active until they are approved
  check-updates  List the plugins whose catalog ref or package moved
  run            Runs a command a plugin registered (`cli_commands`), or lists them
  hooks          Shell hooks, gateway hook directories and outbound webhooks
  diff-grants    The capabilities a staged update asks for beyond the current grant
  remove         Remove an installed plugin (its grants are revoked; its data in `plugin-data/` is kept)
  grants         Show, approve or revoke a plugin's capability grants
  capabilities   Declared versus granted capabilities, per plugin
  adopt          Register a plugin directory placed by hand in the profile's `plugins/`: validate it, record it as `adopted` and approve its capabilities
  validate       Check a plugin directory: manifest, WIT world compatibility and capability declarations (exit 65 on any error)
  pack           Pack a plugin directory into a `.pmtpkg` package
  sign           Sign a package's digest with a minisign secret key: writes `<package>.minisig`
  doctor         Problems of the profile's plugins: load errors, unsigned or unadopted plugins, plugins modified after install or removed from the catalog
  reload         Replace the profile's plugin instances (in the running daemon when there is one): hooks, slash commands and event subscribers change at once, tools and system-prompt sections in sessions started afterwards (`/plugins reload --now` applies them to a session)
  test-adapter   Run the adapter conformance kit against a mock of the platform: a first-party platform name (`telegram`, `discord`, `slack`, `email`, `matrix`, `signal`, `whatsapp`, `webhook`; builds with the `adapter-kits` feature) or a `platform-adapter` plugin directory
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus plugins install`

```text
Install a plugin: a catalog id (its pinned ref), a `.pmtpkg` file, or a Git URL with `--ref <full commit SHA>`

Usage: prometheus plugins install [OPTIONS] <IDENTIFIER>

Arguments:
  <IDENTIFIER>
          A catalog id, a `.pmtpkg` path or a Git URL

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Prometheus home directory (default: PROMETHEUS_HOME, else ~/.prometheus)

      --ref <SHA>
          The full commit SHA of a Git install

      --allow-unsigned
          Install without a verified signature (recorded on the install record)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Profile to use (default: the home's active_profile, else default)

      --allow-removed
          Install although the catalog removed the plugin (recorded)

      --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

      --enable
          Enable it now (asks to approve its capabilities)

      --json
          Print one JSON document on stdout; errors go to stderr as JSON

      --no-enable
          Leave it disabled

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail; repeatable

      --grant <all|CAPABILITIES>
          With `--enable`: approve `all` requested capabilities, or a list

      --no-color
          No colour (also when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is not a terminal)

      --force
          Install although the threat scan graded it `caution` (recorded); a `dangerous` verdict is refused anyway

  -q, --quiet
          Only the answer: no banner, spinner or tool previews

      --safe-mode
          Start with no plugins, MCP servers, sidecars, hooks or webhooks; a chat also ignores config.toml and rules and needs --model and --provider

      --accept-hooks
          Run shell hooks nobody approved yet (as `hooks.auto_accept`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `prometheus plugins help`

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: prometheus plugins help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  install        Install a plugin: a catalog id (its pinned ref), a `.pmtpkg` file, or a Git URL with `--ref <full commit SHA>`
  search         Catalog entries matching a word
  browse         Every catalog entry, by tier and category
  show           A plugin's details: installed state, worlds, capabilities and provenance, and its catalog entry
  list           Every discovered plugin: id, version, kind, source, state (`loaded`, `disabled`, `unadopted` or `error`) and why it does not load
  enable         Enable a plugin: shows its capabilities and asks you to approve them (non-interactively, `--grant all` or `--grant <cap>,...` approves; otherwise exits 4). It loads in sessions started afterwards
  disable        Disable a plugin (it keeps its grants)
  update         Update a plugin, or every plugin whose catalog ref or package moved; one asking for new capabilities keeps its current version active until they are approved
  check-updates  List the plugins whose catalog ref or package moved
  run            Runs a command a plugin registered (`cli_commands`), or lists them
  hooks          Shell hooks, gateway hook directories and outbound webhooks
  diff-grants    The capabilities a staged update asks for beyond the current grant
  remove         Remove an installed plugin (its grants are revoked; its data in `plugin-data/` is kept)
  grants         Show, approve or revoke a plugin's capability grants
  capabilities   Declared versus granted capabilities, per plugin
  adopt          Register a plugin directory placed by hand in the profile's `plugins/`: validate it, record it as `adopted` and approve its capabilities
  validate       Check a plugin directory: manifest, WIT world compatibility and capability declarations (exit 65 on any error)
  pack           Pack a plugin directory into a `.pmtpkg` package
  sign           Sign a package's digest with a minisign secret key: writes `<package>.minisig`
  doctor         Problems of the profile's plugins: load errors, unsigned or unadopted plugins, plugins modified after install or removed from the catalog
  reload         Replace the profile's plugin instances (in the running daemon when there is one): hooks, slash commands and event subscribers change at once, tools and system-prompt sections in sessions started afterwards (`/plugins reload --now` applies them to a session)
  test-adapter   Run the adapter conformance kit against a mock of the platform: a first-party platform name (`telegram`, `discord`, `slack`, `email`, `matrix`, `signal`, `whatsapp`, `webhook`; builds with the `adapter-kits` feature) or a `platform-adapter` plugin directory
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

```text
          Override a config key for this invocation only; repeatable, never saved

  -m, --model <MODEL>

          More detail; repeatable
```

## `prometheus help`

```text
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: prometheus help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  chat         Talk to the agent: interactive on a terminal, one-shot with `-z` or when stdin or stdout is not a terminal (the default command)
  version      Print the version and build identity (`--json` for every field, `--verbose` for build details and compiled-in surfaces)
  setup        Set up the profile: model and provider (or a subscription sign-in), secrets, tools, terminal and memory
  doctor       Check the install and profile: one ok / warn / fail line per check; `--fix` performs the enumerated repairs
  debug        Diagnostics: `debug summary` prints a plain-text setup summary for support threads
  config       Read, change, validate and explain the profile's config.toml
  secrets      Store, list and remove the profile's secrets (values never on the command line)
  skills       List, inspect, enable, lint and maintain the profile's skills and skill bundles
  journey      The skills and memories the agent learned, as a timeline; list, delete, edit
  memory       Inspect, edit, export and import what the agent remembers (built-in memory)
  grants       List and revoke the profile's permanent capability grants and approvals
  browser      Browser sessions: status, and closing the real browser whose profile real-profile browsing copies
  lsp          Language servers behind the diagnostics of file edits: status, registry, installs, restart
  cron         Scheduled jobs: create, list, pause, run now, inspect runs, replay, doctor and the headless tick
  worktrees    Git worktrees of sessions and subagents: list, sweep and restore archived trees
  vault        The credential vault: logins, cards and addresses the browser fills by handle
  security     Security records of the profile: verify the tamper-evident audit log
  backup       Back up the whole home to a .tar.zst archive, or restore one
  files        Undo a session's file changes, roll a workspace back to a checkpoint, and manage the file snapshot store
  verify       Detect a project's build/test/start recipe and run it
  snapshots    Snapshot and restore the selected profile's critical state
  profile      List, create, select, rename and delete profiles
  sessions     List, search, export and manage the profile's sessions
  logs         Show structured log records of a component (`list` names them)
  usage        Totals of model and metered tool calls from the usage ledger
  prompt       Measure the system prompt and tool schemas a new session would send
  demo         Run the offline demo: the agent fixes a bug in a small ledger repository with the scripted mock provider, in a temporary profile
  trajectory   Render the recorded trajectory of a session
  model        Pick, set, list and inspect the profile's model (no subcommand: the interactive picker)
  providers    Provider routing state: per-route health scores
  moa          List, create, update and delete Mixture of Agents presets (`[moa.presets.<name>]`)
  fallback     List and edit the profile's fallback chain (`[[fallback.chain]]`)
  auth         Add, list and remove provider API keys and subscription sign-ins (an interactive manager without a subcommand on a terminal)
  tools        List the profile's tools and explain one (exposure, capabilities, approvals)
  toolsets     List toolsets and show the tools a toolset resolves to
  approvals    Check how the approval gate treats a command, without running it
  update       Update this install to its channel's newest signed release, check for one (exit 10 when available), change the channel, or roll back
  pause        Emergency pause: no new turns or scheduled jobs on any profile of this home until `pause off` (running turns finish)
  portal       The Nous Portal subscription and its tool gateway routing
  daemon       Run, start, stop and inspect the gateway daemon that owns this home's sessions (one per home; clients attach to it)
  gateway      Messaging adapters of the running daemon and the profile's delivery outbox
  pairing      Approve, deny, list and revoke messaging senders' pairing requests. A code is approved with `prometheus pairing approve <platform> <code>`, the RPC `pairing.approve` from a client attached to the profile, or the admin-only chat command `/pair approve <code>`
  connectors   Hosted app connectors (Gmail, Notion, Linear...) on the Nous connector gateway: list them, list and rename accounts, connect and disconnect accounts
  bridge       The python bridge: sidecar status, logs and restarts, a doctor for the managed runtime and plugin environments, and named side environments for skill scripts
  mcp          MCP servers: add (from a preset or the catalog), list, remove, test and sign in to the profile's servers, pick their tools, show their state, and serve Prometheus tools and skills to MCP clients. With no subcommand on a terminal, an interactive picker
  plugins      Plugins: list, enable and disable them, manage their capability grants, and run the adapter conformance kit (`plugins test-adapter`)
  tui          The full-screen terminal UI, attached to the home's gateway daemon (started when it is not running), or with `--standalone` to an in-process gateway that serves only this TUI
  schema       Print the JSON Schema of a published contract (`subagent-result`)
  rpc          The daemon's client protocol: `rpc schema` prints the schema this binary speaks
  completions  Print a shell completion script (load it from your shell's startup file, for example `source <(prometheus completions zsh)`)
  runtimes     List, install, verify and collect the managed runtimes (Node, CPython, uv, Chromium) shared by every profile
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

## `prometheus help skills`

```text
List, inspect, enable, lint and maintain the profile's skills and skill bundles

Usage: prometheus help skills [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list             List the profile's skills with category, source and status (shadowed copies marked)
  show             Show one skill: where it comes from, its status, its files and its SKILL.md
  enable           Enable a skill (from the next session)
  disable          Disable a skill (from the next session); `prometheus-agent` cannot be disabled
  lint             Check skills against the authoring rules (all of the profile's when no path is given)
  trust            Load the skills of a git checkout (`.prometheus/skills`, `.agents/skills`) in new sessions
  eject            Copy a bundled skill into the profile as an editable copy that shadows it
  diff             Show how an ejected copy differs from the current bundled version
  reset            Remove an ejected copy so the name resolves to the bundled skill again
  doctor           Report skills that do not load (path, line, reason) and quarantined project skills
  reload           Rescan every skill root and bundle; report added, removed and changed skills since the last reload
  bundles          Manage skill bundles (`<profile>/skill-bundles/<slug>.toml`)
  pending          Review skill writes staged by `skills.write_approval` (default: list them)
  opt-out          Hide every bundled skill from this profile across upgrades (`prometheus-agent` stays)
  opt-in           Show bundled skills again (the default)
  list-modified    List ejected skills whose content differs from their recorded origin
  repair-official  Re-record the provenance of official catalog installs that match the embedded copy
```

## `prometheus help memory`

```text
Inspect, edit, export and import what the agent remembers (built-in memory)

Usage: prometheus help memory [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status   Show whether built-in memory is enabled, each store's usage and pending changes
  list     List entries (dormant ones only with --all)
  show     Show one entry in full (blocked entries show their raw text here)
  add      Add an entry (from the next session's snapshot)
  rm       Remove an entry
  pin      Pin an entry
  unpin    Unpin an entry
  edit     Edit entries as Markdown in $VISUAL / $EDITOR; the result is applied as one batch after showing the diff
  export   Print every entry as Markdown (the edit view) or JSONL
  import   Import a Markdown or JSONL export, or a Hermes MEMORY.md / USER.md (entries separated by §)
  pending  List memory changes staged for approval
  approve  Apply a staged change (`all` for every one)
  reject   Drop a staged change (`all` for every one)
  log      List memory revisions, oldest first
  diff     Show memory changes as a unified diff per entry
  revert   Undo a revision (recorded as a new revision with origin user)
  search   Rank archival entries for a query as recall would
  setup    Set up an external memory provider: its settings go to config.toml, its secrets to the secrets store; takes effect from the next session
  off      Use built-in memory only (memory.provider = "builtin")
  reset    Delete every entry of a store
```

## `prometheus help cron`

```text
Scheduled jobs: create, list, pause, run now, inspect runs, replay, doctor and the headless tick

Usage: prometheus help cron [COMMAND]

Commands:
  list         The jobs: id, name, schedule, state, next run and last status
  add          Create a job; the schedule is echoed with its next three instants and saved only after confirmation
  edit         Change a job; a new schedule is echoed and confirmed again
  pause        Stop a job from firing until it is resumed
  resume       Fire a paused job again, from now
  run          Run a job now, in the foreground (its schedule and state are untouched)
  remove       Delete a job (its run records are kept under run retention)
  runs         A job's runs, newest first
  show-run     One run in full: times, status, error, session, cost and output
  replay       Re-execute a recorded run without delivering it
  incidents    Failure incidents, newest activity first; `ack <id>` silences one
  notepad      A job's notepad: `list` (default), `get <key>`, `set <key> <value>`, `delete <key>`
  suggestions  Suggested automations: `list` (default), `accept <n> [--yes]`, `dismiss <n>`, `catalog` (adds the curated starters), `clear`
  status       Job counts, the next due job and who ticks the profile
  doctor       Trigger, tick lease, due-but-unfired occurrences, jobs in error, undelivered outbox rows and every `cron.*` setting; exits 1 when a job is in error or a delivery outcome is unknown
  tick         Run one tick in this process (for OS schedulers); does nothing while a gateway daemon owns scheduling
```

## `prometheus help sessions`

```text
List, search, export and manage the profile's sessions

Usage: prometheus help sessions [COMMAND]

Commands:
  browse           Pick a session interactively (status tags, search) and resume it
  resume           Resume a session (id, id prefix or title) in a chat; a turn the process stopped during is resumed, closed or offered by `agent.resume_on_crash`
  list             List sessions, most recently active first
  show             Show a session (id, id prefix or title)
  search           Full-text search over the profile's messages
  rename           Set a session's title
  pin              Pin a session (pinned sessions are never pruned)
  unpin            Unpin a session
  archive          Archive a session (hidden from the default listing)
  unarchive        Unarchive a session
  tree             Show a session's lineage tree (forks, continuations, delegates)
  fork             Fork a session: a new session with its active messages up to --at
  siblings         List the other children of a session's parent (forks, continuations)
  import           Import a JSONL export (all-or-none; ids must be new unless --remap-ids)
  recover          Copy every readable row of state.db into a new clean store (needs the store closed)
  journal-mode     Switch state.db's journal mode offline (delete for filesystems without shared memory)
  refresh-prompts  Rebuild the stored system prompt of sessions at their next turn
  retitle          Regenerate automatic titles with the title model (user titles are kept)
  stats            Show a session's and its lineage's message and token totals
  export           Export sessions (jsonl, md, html, prompts or trace)
  delete           Delete a session (asks for confirmation unless --yes)
  prune            Delete ended, unpinned sessions inactive for longer than --older-than days
  rewind           Rewind a session to a user message (soft delete; --restore undoes it)
  repair           Rebuild the derived search indexes from the stored messages
  vacuum           Compact state.db and truncate its write-ahead log
```

## `prometheus help auth`

```text
Add, list and remove provider API keys and subscription sign-ins (an interactive manager without a subcommand on a terminal)

Usage: prometheus help auth [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add       Store an API key (read from a hidden prompt or stdin) or sign in to a subscription
  list      List every credential: provider, label, kind, source and status (never key or token material)
  status    One provider's credentials, sign-in flows and plan notes
  remove    Delete a credential (and revoke a sign-in's refresh token where the provider offers revocation)
  priority  Move an API key of the pool to a 0-based position (the order `fill_first` takes them in); the others are renumbered
  reset     Clear benches and cooldowns (every credential of the provider, or one); running sessions use them on their next request
  refresh   Refresh sign-in tokens now and return them to rotation
  logout    Remove every subscription sign-in of a provider
  usage     Show a subscription's account usage windows without starting a session (exit 1 when nothing can be shown)
  import    Copy another tool's sign-in into the secrets store
```

## `prometheus help daemon`

```text
Run, start, stop and inspect the gateway daemon that owns this home's sessions (one per home; clients attach to it)

Usage: prometheus help daemon [COMMAND]

Commands:
  run                Run the daemon in the foreground (what `start` launches)
  start              Start the daemon in the background; does nothing when it runs
  ensure             Start the daemon when it is not running and print its endpoint (with `--json`: one object for clients that spawn it)
  stop               Stop the daemon after its running turns finish
  restart            Replace the daemon (after a binary update): drain running turns, stop it and start this binary's daemon
  status             Print the daemon's process state
  install-service    Install a per-user supervisor unit that starts the daemon at login (no administrator rights); `--system --run-as-user` installs a boot-time unit instead (root only)
  uninstall-service  Stop and remove the unit `install-service` installed
```

## `prometheus help gateway`

```text
Messaging adapters of the running daemon and the profile's delivery outbox

Commands:

  slack-manifest  Print (or write) a Slack app manifest for Socket Mode with one slash command per gateway command
  whatsapp        WhatsApp linked-device setup
  pause           Stop dispatching one adapter's inbound messages (they are acknowledged and dropped) without disconnecting it; kept across restarts
  resume          Clear an adapter's pause and reconnect backoff and reconnect it now
```

## `prometheus help mcp`

```text
MCP servers: add (from a preset or the catalog), list, remove, test and sign in to the profile's servers, pick their tools, show their state, and serve Prometheus tools and skills to MCP clients. With no subcommand on a terminal, an interactive picker

Usage: prometheus help mcp [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add      Add a server: `--command <program> [--args ...]` for a local (stdio) server run in the sandbox, `--url <url>` for a streamable HTTP server, or `--preset <name>`; the server is probed and, on a terminal, its tool checklist offered. Its tools join sessions started afterwards
  list     Every configured server: transport, command or URL, trust and whether it is enabled
  remove   Remove a server
  test     Start a server and list its tools: handshake, tool count and latency (exit 69 when it does not answer)
  tools    Re-open a server's tool checklist; writes `tools.include` only when not every tool is selected
  login    Sign in to an `auth = "oauth"` server (prints the authorization URL; paste the redirect URL when the browser cannot reach this machine)
  reauth   Forget a server's sign-in and sign in again
  catalog  The MCP servers of the plugin catalog
  install  Install an MCP server from the catalog (disabled until you enable it)
  status   Start every enabled server and show its state, tool count and why it is unavailable
  serve    Serve this profile's `mcp_server.expose_toolsets` (default: the read-only skill tools) as MCP tools and its skills as MCP prompts and resources, on stdio or streamable HTTP
```

## `prometheus help plugins`

```text
Plugins: list, enable and disable them, manage their capability grants, and run the adapter conformance kit (`plugins test-adapter`)

Usage: prometheus help plugins [COMMAND]

Commands:
  install        Install a plugin: a catalog id (its pinned ref), a `.pmtpkg` file, or a Git URL with `--ref <full commit SHA>`
  search         Catalog entries matching a word
  browse         Every catalog entry, by tier and category
  show           A plugin's details: installed state, worlds, capabilities and provenance, and its catalog entry
  list           Every discovered plugin: id, version, kind, source, state (`loaded`, `disabled`, `unadopted` or `error`) and why it does not load
  enable         Enable a plugin: shows its capabilities and asks you to approve them (non-interactively, `--grant all` or `--grant <cap>,...` approves; otherwise exits 4). It loads in sessions started afterwards
  disable        Disable a plugin (it keeps its grants)
  update         Update a plugin, or every plugin whose catalog ref or package moved; one asking for new capabilities keeps its current version active until they are approved
  check-updates  List the plugins whose catalog ref or package moved
  run            Runs a command a plugin registered (`cli_commands`), or lists them
  hooks          Shell hooks, gateway hook directories and outbound webhooks
  diff-grants    The capabilities a staged update asks for beyond the current grant
  remove         Remove an installed plugin (its grants are revoked; its data in `plugin-data/` is kept)
  grants         Show, approve or revoke a plugin's capability grants
  capabilities   Declared versus granted capabilities, per plugin
  adopt          Register a plugin directory placed by hand in the profile's `plugins/`: validate it, record it as `adopted` and approve its capabilities
  validate       Check a plugin directory: manifest, WIT world compatibility and capability declarations (exit 65 on any error)
  pack           Pack a plugin directory into a `.pmtpkg` package
  sign           Sign a package's digest with a minisign secret key: writes `<package>.minisig`
  doctor         Problems of the profile's plugins: load errors, unsigned or unadopted plugins, plugins modified after install or removed from the catalog
  reload         Replace the profile's plugin instances (in the running daemon when there is one): hooks, slash commands and event subscribers change at once, tools and system-prompt sections in sessions started afterwards (`/plugins reload --now` applies them to a session)
  test-adapter   Run the adapter conformance kit against a mock of the platform: a first-party platform name (`telegram`, `discord`, `slack`, `email`, `matrix`, `signal`, `whatsapp`, `webhook`; builds with the `adapter-kits` feature) or a `platform-adapter` plugin directory
```


## JSON output

With `--json` a command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout (JSON Lines for `--follow` streams) and nothing else; diagnostics go to stderr. A failing command prints `{"error": {kind, code, message, hint}}` to stderr and exits with its [exit code](error-codes.md). Listing and status documents carry a top-level `schema` naming their versioned shape; a breaking change bumps the shape's major version. `version --json` is the fixed build-identity object and has no `schema` field.

|---|---|
| `prometheus.profile_export.v1` | `prometheus profile export` |
| `prometheus.doctor.v1` | `prometheus doctor` |
| `prometheus.update_status.v1` | `prometheus update --status` |
| `prometheus.update_check.v1` | `prometheus update --check` |
| `prometheus.runtimes.v1` | `prometheus runtimes list` |
| `prometheus.runtimes_verify.v1` | `prometheus runtimes verify` |
| `prometheus.runtimes_doctor.v1` | `prometheus runtimes doctor` |
